title: Cap. VIII Arg.: peccata reprobi sunt causa omnium effectorum — therefore also of reprobation
pass_a_gloss: The sins of the reprobate are the cause of all the effects of reprobation itself: Therefore also of Divine reprobation, as it regards those effects. For as to what pertains to the first effect, namely hardening or the subtraction of peculiar grace, it is plain that it arises from the demerits of antecedent sins: Rom. 1; 2 Thess. 2; Exod. 9. As to what pertains to the last effect, namely eternal damnation, it is plain that its cause is human demerits from the very form of the sentence passed in the final judgment.
pass_b_english: Argument: the sins of the reprobate are the cause of all the effects of reprobation itself; therefore also of divine reprobation as it regards those effects. As to the first effect — hardening or subtraction of peculiar grace — it plainly arises from demerits of antecedent sins (Rom. 1; 2 Thess. 2; Exod. 9). As to the last — eternal damnation — human demerits are plainly its cause from the very form of the sentence passed at the final judgment.
source_text: Peccata reprobi sunt causa omnium effectorum reprobationis ipsius: Ergo etiam reprobationis Divinae, ut respicit illos effectus. Quod enim attinet ad primum effectum, scilicet indurationem seu subtractionem peculiaris gratiae, patet illam ex peccatorum antecedentium demeritis oriri: Rom. i.; 2 Thess. ii.; Exod. ix. Quod attinet ad ultimum effectum, nempe aeternam damnationem, patet ejus causam esse demerita humana ex ipsa forma sententiae latae in judicio finali.
